title: Did you miss @The Festival?  Here’s a full recap of what the weekend ...
transcript: I just got back from the festival, the three day musical theatre festival in upstate New York. So I wanted to do a recap of what the experience was like. The good, the bad, and the ugly. In terms of setup, there were three main stages. They had the main main stage, which had reserved seating for all of the guests that had reserved seating. They had a secondary stage, which had a V I P. Tent, but for the most part, everyone was sitting on the ground. However, there was an option to rent some chairs for an added fee. And then there was a third stage, which was the smallest of the three, a couple of Adirondack chairs, but again, for the most part, people are sitting on the ground or standing in the back. And they also had multiple food offerings, as well as a marketplace. And as with any festival, all three stages had performances going on throughout the day, often overlapping with each other, so it was not possible to see everything. I did a lot of hopping around, so I would catch, like, the first half of one show, the second half of another, and never really had any trouble finding a spot. Although I will caveat that we did have the reserved seats in the main stage, which I think helped a lot. If you did not have reserved seats, you either had to stand in the back or stand along the sides. They Did have one section of unreserved seats off on the side out in the sun, and it was very hot, so not ideal. In terms of the programming. I was really impressed they compiled such a great group of performers, and everyday had at least one a lister, with most of them doing multiple shows throughout the day. So, for example, if you wanted to see Kelly O'hara, she was rapping at the 80s jukebox in the morning, singing bridges with Jason Robert Brown in the middle of the day, singing a few songs in the big show in the evening. The big show being exactly what it sounds like. Their big concert at the end of the day, and then after that, ended the night at the campfire, singing a duet with her daughter and husband. And even in cases where they only were doing one show, like Audra McDonald, she did like an entire 40 minute concert set as part of the big show. I never felt like I wasn't getting enough of these big performers. And it was so clear just how much fun they were all having. You could really see what a community this is. And like, you would be watching Lena Hall absolutely crush it. And then on the sides of the stage were Jenna Collela, Renee, Elise Goldsberry and Kelly O'hara watching in awe and hyping her up. And of course, the biggest piece of programming was the rent reunion on Saturday. You Had 13 of the 15 original cast members of rent reuniting, singing a bunch of songs from the show, telling some stories. It was so special and like that alone was worth the price of admission. But I will say going into this I had no idea what to expect. They had never done one before and it felt like it could either be a disaster or it could be really cool. And I'm happy to report that it ended up being really cool and for a first time event, ended up being really well run. Things ran mostly on time, it was never too crowded and the performances were all incredible. I was genuinely so sad to leave and thankfully they've already announced that it's coming back next year, so I can't wait to do it all over again, but I don't know if anything will quite have the magic that this first year did.
